name: Yadgir
headline: Distress migration pulls 14-18-year-olds out of school; the Deputy Commissioner drives dropouts back herself.
summary: Yadgir's sources describe mass distress migration of labourer families to cities such as Bengaluru, a survey finding 1,747 out-of-school children aged 14-18, and a 2019 count of 1,547 children absent for more than three weeks, the highest in the state at the time. The administration uses NIOS and 'Mitra' programmes to bring older adolescents back, and an Azim Premji action-research study points to economic constraints at the transition into secondary school.

reasons.detail: Families unable to live off arid land migrate to cities for construction and wage work, taking children out of school.
In 2019 Yadgir had the state's highest number of children missing school for over three consecutive weeks.
Yadgir managed 54.43% in 2024 and 51.6% in 2025; the district Zilla Panchayat CEO issued a circular tying teacher increments to subject results.

reasons.factor: Economic bottleneck at the move to secondary school
reasons.detail: Azim Premji Foundation research found deep-rooted economic constraints blocking the transition into secondary school.

Officials interpreting the 2019 state absenteeism survey, where Yadgir had the second-highest count, named migration and illness as main reasons; the 2018-19 survey also cited migration and disinterest.
Yadgir has a 25.38% multidimensional poverty rate and the lowest district output in the state; an educator notes labourers can lack work for months, and parents take children to fields.
An RTE activist says teacher shortages are most severe in Kalyana Karnataka districts including Yadgir; a teacher also describes absent teachers going unpenalised across the region.
A social worker describes girls withdrawn from school and married off; in August 2025 a Class 9 girl gave birth in a Shahapur residential school washroom, prompting a child rights inquiry.

responses.text: The administration uses NIOS and 'Mitra' programmes to mainstream older out-of-school adolescents; the Deputy Commissioner personally returns dropouts to class.
Yadgir Zilla Panchayat's CEO circular (2024) withheld annual increments from subject teachers below the district pass percentage; teachers' association objected.
After the Shahapur residential school incident the state child rights commission ordered an inquiry and counselling; the hostel warden was suspended.
